title: Denver Breakfast Casserole
subtitle: Ham, bell peppers, and onion baked into a make-ahead egg strata.
description: Ham, bell peppers, onion, and cheddar baked with eggs — the Denver omelette in casserole form for ten hungry firefighters.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Denver Breakfast Casserole in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Double-check seasoning after scaling — crew palates run salty after long shifts, so taste the first portion before opening the line. Use diced ham, shredded cheddar as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Toast the bread cubes
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 350°F. Spread bread cubes on a sheet pan and toast 6–8 minutes until dry at the edges. Cool slightly so they don't turn the custard soggy.

steps.title: Build the pan
steps.instruction: Butter a deep 9x13 dish. Layer half the bread, ham, peppers, onion, and half the cheese. Repeat layers, finishing with cheese on top.

steps.title: Whisk the custard
steps.instruction: Whisk eggs with milk, dry mustard, salt, pepper, and a pinch of paprika until smooth. Pour evenly over the bread—press gently so cubes soak without compacting.

steps.title: Rest or refrigerate
steps.instruction: Rest 30 minutes at room temperature, or cover and refrigerate overnight for a true make-ahead. Bring closer to room temp before baking if chilled.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Denver Breakfast Casserole onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Bake until set
steps.instruction: Bake at 375°F until puffed, golden at the edges, and a knife inserted in the center comes out clean. Rest 10 minutes before cutting into squares for the line.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Denver Breakfast Casserole — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

stationWorkflow: Prep and refrigerate the casserole the night before a busy shift; pull it 30 minutes before baking.
Assign one cook to oven checks while another sets up a warm holding pan with foil for staggered eaters.
Cut with a sharp serrated knife in the pan, then lift squares with a offset spatula to keep layers intact.
cleanupNotes: Soak the 9x13 in warm soapy water immediately after serving—egg custard bonds to metal if left to dry.
Line the sheet pan with parchment when toasting bread cubes for a one-wipe cleanup.
leftovers: Wrap individual squares in foil and reheat at 325°F for 12 minutes until steaming in the center.
Dice cold casserole into a breakfast fried rice with soy, green onion, and a fried egg on top.
